speaker_role: independent counselor (College Coach, a paid admissions consulting company)
commercial_incentive: Yes - produced by College Coach, a paid college admissions consulting firm, though the video itself is informational rather than a direct pitch
key_insights: Most standardized testing happens before students finalize their college list, so many students test even without knowing final test-optional status of target schools
If none of a student's target colleges require scores, or the student feels the transcript is stronger than test results, skipping test prep/submission can be reasonable
To decide whether to submit scores to test-optional schools, look up the college's Common Data Set to find the middle-50% test score range of admitted students
If a score is above the school's average range, submitting it can enhance the application; if below average, it's better not to submit
At genuinely test-optional schools, choosing not to submit scores will not negatively affect the application
notable_or_distinctive: Provides a clear, actionable method (searching '[college name] + common data set' to find the admitted middle-50% test range) for making the submit/don't-submit decision, rather than just generic advice.
reliability_notes: Generic but practically useful and consistent with standard admissions consulting advice; no data or citations beyond referring students to look up common data sets themselves; produced by a paid consulting firm but not a hard sales pitch.
